patch.value: An extension command that declares no flags hands every undeclared option to its handler, although the dynamic validator documents refusing them

Found while fixing pm-gh1666 on 2026.11.7. An extension registers demo-plain with registerCommand and no registerFlags. pm demo-plain --bogus --json exits 0 and the handler receives options.bogus = true; pm demo-plain --all --json delivers options.all = true. validateDynamicExtensionCommandOptions in src/cli/runtime/invocation-options.ts is documented to reject all supplied options when a command declares no flags, and cli-main-errors.spec asserts that refusal on the function directly, but the built CLI never reaches it with these options. A command with declared flags refuses the same spellings as unknown options, so the two shapes disagree. The unknown-option refusal on a command with flags also lists --no-extensions and the read-output controls as expected flags, although a non-read extension command refuses them. Duplicate check: searched undeclared option, no flags, dynamic validator and unknown option across all statuses; pm-in23qu and pm-8nyc own unknown-option suggestions, not this leak.

pm <cmd> --bogus on an extension command that declares no flags exits 2 with an unknown-option refusal naming the command, and the handler never runs; Root-only flags (--all, --explain) are refused the same way unless the command declares them; The unknown-option refusal on an extension command lists only the flags that command accepts: its declared flags plus its inherited host flags from pm contracts, not --no-extensions or read-output controls on a non-read command; An integration spec drives the built CLI for both command shapes, with a negative control that bypasses the validator
Register demo-plain with registerCommand and no flags, then run pm demo-plain --bogus --json
exit 2 unknown-option refusal; the handler does not run
exit 0 and the handler receives options.bogus = true

value.text: Root cause located (2026-11-07, while fixing a Codex review finding on the pm-gh1665/1666/1667 batch): wrapProgramActionsForExtensionHandlers in src/cli/main.ts wraps every Commander action and calls runActiveCommandHandler for a registered extension handler BEFORE the dynamic command action runs. validateDynamicExtensionCommandOptions lives only in that dynamic action (runRequiredExtensionCommand), so for a handler-backed command it is never reached. A command with declared flags is still guarded because extractCommandScopedOptions validates loose options against its definitions; a command with no flags is not. The batch PR closes only the root-only subset (--all/--explain) for every extension command, via refuseUndeclaredRootOnlyOptions in the wrapper. The general fix (call the zero-flag option validator in the wrapper) is deliberately left here: it can break packages whose handlers read options they never declared through registerFlags, so it needs a fleet census of package commands that read context.options without declarations, and a migration note.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Re-scoped after a fleet census (2026-11-07). Wiring a zero-flag refusal into the handler dispatch path works on the built CLI (pm demo-plain --bogus exits 2 unknown_option), but a read-only census of all 47 unbraind pm-* repos plus the bundled packages found 13 released zero-flag commands in 8 repos that read options they never declare, and pm-graph parses its flags from context.args (12 of 17 commands). Shipping the refusal now would break those packages for every user, so the handler path keeps passing undeclared options through and the refusal stays here.

Delivered in this batch: child pm-1du7s3 (refusal on commands with declared flags carries code unknown_option and lists only declared plus inherited host flags; the dynamic-path zero-flag refusal gets the same code and list). Prerequisite before the flip: child pm-kl1nio (the package-side migration, with the census table). Once pm-kl1nio lands, wire refuseUndeclaredExtensionCommandOptions into wrapProgramActionsForExtensionHandlers in src/cli/main.ts (it is one call; the census run showed the exact refusal text) and meet AC 1, 2 and 4 here. Options considered and rejected: a stderr warning per invocation (noisy for every pm-graph user who cannot fix the package), and a per-command strict opt-in (new SDK surface that leaves the default lenient forever).
